name: nano-banana-image
cost: Paid API. Most services have a free quota
works_with: Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, Codex, Cursor, Roo Code, Goose and more
short: Makes and edits images with Gemini's Nano Banana models through the AceDataCloud API.
what: Teaches your agent to generate images from text, or edit images you already have, with the Nano Banana models (nano-banana, nano-banana-2-lite, nano-banana-2 and nano-banana-pro) through AceDataCloud. Edits are plain-language instructions with no mask. It supports several aspect ratios and 1K, 2K or 4K output.
who: People who want their agent to produce or touch up images and are happy to use a paid API account. If you already call Google's API directly, you may not need it.
needs: An AceDataCloud account at platform.acedata.cloud with a subscribed service and an API token
Node.js for `npx`, or Claude Code for the plugin route

steps.title: Get a token
steps.text: Register at platform.acedata.cloud, subscribe to a service, create an API credential, then set it in your shell rather than pasting it into chat.

steps.title: Install the skills
steps.text: This installs every AceDataCloud skill. To install only this one, use the README's specific-skills form (`--skill <name>`) with `nano-banana-image`.

steps.title: Or, in Claude Code, install the media plugin
steps.text: nano-banana-image is in the ai-media bundle.

steps.title: Optional: add the MCP server for tool use
steps.text: Or use the hosted endpoint at https://nanobanana.mcp.acedata.cloud/mcp.

try.label: From the SKILL.md
try.text:
curl -X POST https://api.acedata.cloud/nano-banana/images \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACEDATACLOUD_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"action": "generate", "prompt": "a watercolor painting of a French countryside village", "model": "nano-banana"}'

watch: Your prompts and images go through AceDataCloud's servers.
Jobs can run asynchronously. You poll `/nano-banana/tasks` with the task's `id` until the image is ready.
Images to edit are passed as URLs in `image_urls`, so they need to be reachable online.
Installing with `'*'` also adds the connector skills for Gmail, Slack, GitHub and others. Pick single skills if you don't want those.
